content:
Hello, my name is Will Cook, 22, please remove this if it's inappropriate. I made an open-source Lean research environment around eight unsolved Erdos problems (68, 243, 249, 251, 257, 269, 1041, 1049). It's designed cumulatively. What this means is each problem over time accumulates partial results, computations, failed routes, literature, formal statements and explicit scoped open obligations so that subsequent agents or mathematicians can continue from the existing map. This prevents others from having to tread the same trodden ground and is designed to be sort of a group effort.

This isn't meant to be some kind of promotional thing, it's just if nobody uses it it's sort of pointless and I'm not sure how I can get people interested in it. You don't have to actually clone the repo but you can check out the short papers, which were designed around Terence Tao's guidance for digestion, I guess this is like pre-digestion. It's just writing up the actual underlying mathematical takeaways that the much broader corpus was boiled down to.

I have comparator, and the important parts are Lean checked, I'm in the process of submitting to Palomar. I'm not sure what else I could be doing but I'd love any guidance or critique.

The repo itself is: https://github.com/wcook04/plectis-erdos

I built a website to make the maths a bit more manageable for people who are only interested in the maths here: https://wcook04.github.io/plectis/maths/index.html

Thank you, and apologies again if this is the wrong place to be posting this I don't want to break any rules but I thought maybe some people would find it an interesting prototype. There is a lot more but I'm trying to follow the digestion principles even in this release by cutting it down to just interesting "signal" I suppose.
